nutshell: Text-to-image person re-ID (TIReID) fails when user text queries omit fine-grained details, leaving trained cross-modal models unable to distinguish visually similar candidates. ICL adds a test-time module (THI) that asks an MLLM human-centered visual questions about top-ranked candidate images across multiple rounds to refine and enrich the query text for re-ranking, plus a training-time data augmentation strategy (RDA) that uses the same MLLM to enrich, decompose, and recombine training captions for a richer, more diverse training signal - both layered on top of an existing frozen TIReID backbone (RDE) rather than replacing it.
contributions: Test-time Human-centered Interaction (THI): a plug-and-play module that performs K rounds of MLLM-based visual question answering (anchor localization via yes/no questions, then attribute-focused VQA) against top-ranked candidate images, merges the answers into a refined query, and re-ranks via a weighted similarity blend (Eq. 6) - all without retraining the underlying retrieval model.

Reorganization Data Augmentation (RDA): uses the MLLM to enrich each training caption with VQA-derived details, decompose it into attribute-specific sub-sentences, rewrite each into multiple paraphrases, then randomly reorder/recombine them into diverse augmented training texts.

An efficiency scheme for THI that skips interaction for queries whose Top-1 candidate similarity already exceeds a threshold and are confirmed correct in round 1, interacting only with genuinely ambiguous queries in later rounds, motivated by an empirical similarity-vs-correctness analysis (Fig. 3).

LoRA-based supervised fine-tuning of the MLLM (Qwen2-VL-7B-Instruct) specifically for the anchor-localization yes/no task, intended to counter the domain gap between generic MLLM pretraining data and ReID imagery.

Consistent gains when THI/RDA are layered onto RDE across three coarse-grained benchmarks (CUHK-PEDES, ICFG-PEDES, RSTPReid) and one fine-grained benchmark (UFine6926), plus demonstrated transferability of THI alone onto CLIP and IRRA backbones (Table 5) and strong cross-dataset generalization gains (Tables 3-4).
deficiencies: The paper's own ablation (Table 6) shows removing the LoRA domain-adaptation fine-tuning costs only about 1.5 Rank-1 points (#1 77.91 vs. #2 76.38 on CUHK-PEDES; 70.55 vs. 69.00 on RSTPReid) - a fairly small gap given Section 3.2 explicitly motivates LoRA SFT by arguing off-the-shelf MLLM answers on ReID images are 'often unreliable' due to domain gap. Most of THI's benefit appears to come from the general-purpose MLLM interaction itself, not the domain-specific tuning the paper frames as necessary.

Table 1 explicitly reports that THI improves Rank-1 but 'slightly degraded Rank-5 and Rank-10,' attributed to anchor-localization errors accumulating over rounds with no correction mechanism - once a candidate is (possibly wrongly) confirmed as the anchor via a binary yes/no MLLM judgment, its extracted attributes are irreversibly merged into the query used for re-ranking, with no fallback if that judgment was wrong.

Section 3.2 ('Efficient Re-ranking') explicitly frames MLLM inference cost as 'a factor that needs to be considered,' but the paper only reduces the *count* of interactions via a similarity threshold - it never reports actual latency, throughput, or wall-clock comparisons between THI-augmented retrieval and the base retrieval-only pipeline, so the practical cost of deploying multi-round MLLM interaction at retrieval time is never quantified.

All four benchmark galleries are modest in scale (low thousands of test images); there is no experiment at the larger gallery sizes the introduction's own motivating use case (video surveillance) would imply, which is exactly where the K-round, per-query MLLM interaction cost would become most significant.
notable: ICL is purely a plug-and-play wrapper: the underlying cross-modal backbone (RDE) is used completely unchanged ('we do not modify any settings of RDE'), and all reported gains come from the two add-on modules layered on top - worth knowing since Table 5 shows THI alone transfers with smaller but consistent gains onto other backbones (CLIP, IRRA) without retraining them either. Also notable: the NAM baseline results in Table 1's group ❷ (ReID-domain pre-training) are marked as 'reproduced by us' rather than taken from the original NAM paper, which is worth double-checking if citing that specific comparison number.
